extracted.intended_audience: K–12 and other educational institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decision-makers, and legal counsel implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for how recipients (particularly elementary and secondary schools and non-postsecondary recipients) must conduct Title IX formal complaint investigations, adjudications, hearings, confidentiality, training, and appeals. Focuses on separating investigator and decision-maker functions, optionality of hearings for K–12, written question procedures, and protections for minors and complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings optional for elementary and secondary schools (§106.45(b)(6)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: “The recipient's grievance process may, but need not, provide for a hearing.” §106.45(b)(6)(ii) applies to elementary and secondary schools and other recipients that are not postsecondary institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declines to mandate live hearings or cross-examination for elementary and secondary schools; leaving hearings optional preserves local flexibility (e.g., for high school students or students above a certain age). The rule was revised to more clearly state optionality and to apply to non-postsecondary recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written submission of questions after investigative report
rubrics_metrics.description: With or without a hearing, after the recipient has sent the investigative report to the parties and before reaching a determination regarding responsibility, decision-makers must afford each party the opportunity to submit written, relevant questions to be asked of any party or witness, provide each party with the answers, and allow for additional, limited follow-up questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written questions procedure must occur after the investigative report is sent and may overlap with the parties' ten-day period to submit a response to the investigative report (§106.45(b)(5)(vii)) so that the procedure need not extend the grievance timeline. Recipients may set reasonable limits on follow-up questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker must explain exclusion of irrelevant questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers are required to explain the reason for excluding any question proposed by a party as not relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is intended to ensure parties understand why a question was excluded and to promote confidence that perspectives and evidence were appropriately considered. The Department declined to remove this requirement even though commenters noted it may be burdensome in K–12 contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rape shield protections with two exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and evidence about a complainant's prior sexual behavior or predisposition are not relevant unless offered to (1) prove someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct, or (2) prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department retained this rape-shield language (including both exceptions) and clarified it applies to elementary and secondary schools and other non-postsecondary recipients; relevance of consent may depend on State law and ages of parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of identities (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must keep confidential the identity of any individual who has made a report or complaint of sex discrimination, including complainants, respondents, and witnesses, except as permitted by FERPA, as required by law, or to carry out the purposes of 34 CFR part 106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department asserts §106.71 protects against disclosure of identities and disagrees that the grievance process will result in confidential information being shared with 'countless individuals.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may train investigators in child- and disability-sensitive interview techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations do not preclude training investigators in effective interview techniques applicable to children or to individuals with disabilities, including trauma-informed practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department recognizes best practices for interviewing child sexual abuse victims and permits recipients to train Title IX personnel accordingly; the regulations also seek to minimize repeated interviews by not requiring live hearings for K–12.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to compel witness participation; protection from retaliation (§106.71(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the regulations authorizes recipients to compel witness participation; individuals are protected from retaliation for participating or refusing to participate in a Title IX proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges peer pressure concerns in youth contexts and clarifies witnesses cannot be forced to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of single investigator model / separation of functions (§106.45(b)(7)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision-maker must be different from any person who served as the Title IX Coordinator or investigator; recipients may not use a 'single investigator' or 'investigator-only' model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation of investigative and adjudicative functions reduces risk of confirmation bias, promotes checks and balances, improves reliability of fact-finding, and increases fairness and public confidence. No change from final rule; commenters' alternative (hybrid models) were considered but rejected as insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative report must fairly summarize all relevant evidence (§106.45(b)(5)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are required to prepare an investigative report that fairly summarizes all relevant evidence gathered during the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This report provides parties and the decision-maker awareness of evidence gathered and supports the separation of roles by enabling a decision-maker unfamiliar with the investigation to evaluate the matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and ability to assert bias or conflict of interest (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations require recipients to offer appeals for both parties and explicitly permit either party to assert that the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decision-maker had a conflict of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals and bias assertions are complementary safeguards to reinforce fairness and address alleged partiality during investigation or adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker may evaluate credibility without live cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Although observing demeanor is not possible without live cross-examination, a decision-maker may still judge credibility based on factors such as plausibility and consistency in statements; specialized legal training is not required to evaluate credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department rejects the assertion that only live cross-examination allows credibility determinations, noting jurors routinely make credibility judgments without legal training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may set reasonable limits on 'limited follow-up questions' and adopt decorum rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision requires 'limited follow-up questions' and leaves recipients discretion to set reasonable limits; recipients may adopt rules of decorum (e.g., forbidding profanity or ad hominem attacks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-makers must permit only relevant questions and explain exclusions. Rules adopted for use in a Title IX grievance process (other than those required by §106.45) must apply equally to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with law enforcement / permissible temporary delays for good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Good cause may exist to temporarily delay the Title IX grievance process to coordinate or cooperate with a concurrent law enforcement investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations contemplate intersection with criminal investigations and permit limited delays where necessary to protect investigative integrity or safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional hearings regardless of State law; federal regs control in conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaving hearings optional reduces conflicts with State laws prescribing hearings; if a recipient cannot comply with both State law and these final regulations, the Federal regulations control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain discretion to adopt hearing models appropriate to their operations; final regulations clarified definitions of 'postsecondary institution' and 'elementary and secondary school' to delineate applicability of hearing provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training materials must not rely on sex stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any materials used to train Title IX personnel must not rely on sex stereotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of the broader impartiality and training requirements to promote reliability and fairness in fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents/guardians retain legal rights to act for minor parties (§106.6(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the regulations changes or limits the legal rights of parents or guardians to act on behalf of a party; §106.6(g) acknowledges parental/legal guardian roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declines to specify whether a parent writing questions/answers on behalf of a student must consult the child; recipients retain discretion to adopt rules addressing decorum and relevance to mitigate parental disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules used in the grievance process must apply equally to both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any rules adopted by a recipient for use in a Title IX grievance process, other than those required under §106.45, must apply equally to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This equality requirement constrains recipient discretion when creating procedures and decorum rules, ensuring parity between complainant and respondent.
